title: Welcome to ALA Philippines
primary_topics: Welcome address as ALA Philippines Chairman at the inaugural of the ASEAN Law Institute (AsnLI), April 13, 2019 -- the culmination of years of ALA Philippines advocacy to establish the AsnLI

ALA Philippines' central role in establishing the AsnLI: commissioned concept paper by Prof. Andre Palacios, sponsored creation at ALA Governing Council meetings, donated $100,000 as seed money, hosted the inaugural
Introduction and tribute to ALA President and Singapore CJ Sundaresh Menon -- described as 'the most powerful chief justice in the world' under Singapore's constitutional appointment authority
The inauguration of the Philippine delegation's ALA leadership lineage: Angara (founding president), Fernan (second Filipino president), Cruz (third; now AsnLI Chairman)
sub_topics: CJ Sundaresh Menon: triple capacities -- CJ of Singapore, ALA President, Chairman of the Council of ASEAN Chief Justices; CJP's opinion that Singapore's CJ is 'the most powerful in the world' because under the Singapore Constitution he is authorized to appoint all other justices and judges (though PM and Parliament theoretically have veto, historically no appointee has been rejected)
Newly-elected AsnLI officers: Ave Cruz as Chairman, Justice Lee Siew Kin as Vice Chairman, Prof. Andre Palacios as Executive Director

Ave Cruz's title explanation: President Duterte wanted Ave to join government; Cruz declined all juicy positions at senior age ('no longer wanted the stresses and headaches'); Duterte named him Special Envoy to the EU with rank of Ambassador, without compensation, as a roving trouble shooter -- 'an ambassador without having to be stationed abroad and without abandoning his Philippine home'
Cruz also chairs the San Beda University Law Alumni Association -- 'the most sought after recruitment agency for appointment to senior positions in the Philippine government'
Past ALA Presidents in attendance: Justice Chao Hick Tin, the Honorable T.P.B. Menon, and Ave Cruz (immediate past)

Diplomatic corps welcomed: Ambassador Sung Yong Kim (US), Ambassador Gerald Ho Wei Hong (Singapore), Ambassador Song Kane Luangmuninthone (Laos), Ambassador Win Naing (Myanmar); Deputy Head of EU Delegation Thomas Wiersing; Deputy Chief of Mission China Tan Qingsheng; officials of Russia, Cambodia, Malaysia and Thailand
Salvador 'Bing Bong' Medialdea: Executive Secretary -- 'Little President'; old ALA hand, member of Philippine delegation at Singapore ALA General Assembly; San Beda Law Alumni recruit
CJ Lucas P. Bersamin: incumbent CJ of the Philippines; honorary chairman of ALA Philippines; part of Singapore ALA delegation; out of town but returning tonight

Danilo Concepcion: UP President and immediate past law dean; 'prospective entry a membership in our Supreme Court is momentarily postponed till he finishes his term as president of the premier state university in 2023'
ALA Philippines' $100,000 donation: seed money drawn from Tessie Sy-Coson's P6 million contribution to ALA Philippines two years ago (mentioned in SC046 companion)
ALA Philippines pledge: to continue supporting the AsnLI 'with the steadfast cooperation and equal backing of the other ALA members'

stances.claim: The Singapore Chief Justice is 'the most powerful in the world' because under the Singapore Constitution he is authorized to appoint all other justices and judges -- and while PM and Parliament theoretically have veto power, historically no appointee has been rejected. This observation is made as a tribute to CJ Menon, not as a criticism of Singapore's system.
stances.rhetorical_move: constitutional-comparative tribute: using Singapore's unique judicial appointment power to honor the visiting CJ as the world's most institutionally powerful judicial officer

stances.claim: ALA Philippines is the architect of the AsnLI -- commissioning the concept paper (Palacios), sponsoring creation at Governing Council meetings, donating $100,000 as seed money, and hosting the inaugural. The Philippines' leading role in ASEAN legal cooperation is embedded in the institution's origin story.
stances.rhetorical_move: institutional-ownership argument: the Philippines' founding contributions as the basis for its continued leadership claim in ASEAN legal cooperation

notable_anecdotes: The Singapore CJ's appointment power: 'under the Singapore Constitution, he [the CJ] is authorized to appoint all other justices and judges. Though the government, meaning the Prime Minister and Parliament, theoretically have veto power, historically, no appointee has been rejected.' CJP's conclusion: the most powerful CJ in the world.

Ave Cruz as unpaid ambassador without leaving home: 'Duterte wanted Ave to join government but he respectfully declined all the juicy positions offered him because, at his senior age, he no longer wanted the stresses and headaches connected with government service. But his former student, the President, would not just let him go and named him Special Envoy to the European Union, with the rank of Ambassador, without compensation, to act as his roving trouble shooter.' -- An ambassador without a posting, without pay, and without leaving the Philippines.

Danilo Concepcion's SC ambition publicly noted: CJP remarks that Concepcion's 'prospective entry a membership in our Supreme Court is momentarily postponed till he finishes his term as president of the premier state university in 2023' -- a rare public acknowledgment of a future appointment prospect.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered April 13, 2019 as the welcome address at the inaugural of the ASEAN Law Institute (AsnLI) -- hosted by ALA Philippines -- this speech by CJP as ALA Philippines Chairman opens by greeting CJ Sundaresh Menon in his triple capacities as Singapore CJ, ALA President and Council of ASEAN Chief Justices Chairman, observing that 'the Chief Justice of Singapore is the most powerful in the world' because under Singapore's Constitution he is authorized to appoint all other justices and judges, with no appointee historically rejected despite theoretical PM/Parliament veto. He congratulates the newly-elected AsnLI officers: Ave Cruz as Chairman (explained as President Duterte's 'former student' who declined all government offers until Duterte made him 'Special Envoy to the EU, with rank of Ambassador, without compensation, to act as his roving trouble shooter -- an ambassador without having to be stationed abroad and without abandoning his Philippine home'), Justice Lee Siew Kin as Vice Chairman, and Prof. Andre Palacios as Executive Director. He welcomes the diplomatic corps (US, Singapore, Laos, Myanmar ambassadors; EU, China deputy heads), Executive Secretary 'Bing Bong' Medialdea ('Little President'), honorary ALA Philippines chairman CJ Lucas Bersamin, and UP President Danilo Concepcion (whose 'prospective entry to the Supreme Court is momentarily postponed till he finishes his term as UP President in 2023'). He closes by affirming ALA Philippines' central role -- commissioning the concept paper, sponsoring the creation at Governing Council meetings, donating $100,000 as seed money (from Tessie Sy-Coson's P6 million contribution), and pledging continued support: 'Needless to say, we pledge to continue supporting it, and with the steadfast cooperation and equal backing of the other ALA members, we know it will succeed.'
